# Database Transaction Recovery After Power Failure

## Introduction

A database management system (DBMS) promises two things that matter enormously when the lights go out: **durability** (committed transactions survive) and **atomicity** (uncommitted or partially completed transactions leave no trace). Power failure is the canonical crash: the CPU stops mid-instruction, DRAM contents evaporate, and any write that was sitting in an OS or disk cache may or may not have reached stable storage. Recovery is the process by which the DBMS, on restart, reconstructs a consistent state from whatever survived on disk.

# How a Compiler Detects and Optimizes Repeated Expressions

## Introduction

Repeated expressions—subexpressions that appear more than once in a program, or that are invariant across loop iterations—are among the most common sources of wasted computation. A compiler that can recognize and eliminate them can turn an O(n²) loop into an O(n) one, or shave constant factors off hot code.
